description:
Remove the code, configuration and wire formats that nothing in production reaches, along with the shims left behind by finished cutovers. Every later refactor then reads, types and converges less code.

## Background

An audit of the workspace (re-verified at commit 79c177fb) found five groups of dead or compatibility surface.

**Library APIs with no production caller.**
- `crates/jit/src/commands/breakdown.rs` (547 lines) is reached only from tests. It opens one mutation session per child and one per edge.
- `validate_integrity_silent` and its three private helpers (`commands/validate.rs:1835-2640`, about 230 lines) have no caller. They re-implement the integrity checks in `validation/repository.rs`, and one of them opens a git2 repository and resolves working-tree paths against the process cwd (`validate.rs:2471,2521`).
- `drift::enforcement_drift` (`validation/drift.rs:107`) is called only by its own tests.
- Linked-worktree evidence capture is requested only by tests (`CaptureSpec::discover_linked_worktree`, `repository_state/image.rs:719`). Even so, every JSON capture calls `configured_worktree_paths()` (`storage/repository_state_store.rs:597`), which can spawn git.
- In `storage/git_revision.rs`, `changed_paths_between`, `changed_worktree_paths` and `inspect_pinned_target` are called only by tests. A 50-line `clone_git_revision_error` exists because the error type is not `Clone`.
- `check_issue_lease` (`commands/claim.rs:559`) has no caller. Three claim commands declare an unused `<S: IssueStore>`, which forces turbofish calls at `main.rs:8278`, `8353` and `8519`.
- `preview_coverage_rule` (`gate_presets/planning.rs`) and `gate_execution::execute_gate_checker` are reached only by tests. `reusable_verdict` is a one-line passthrough. A gate that is not required is reported three ways: a typed `GateNotRequiredError`, `anyhow!` and `bail!` (`commands/gate.rs:822,1039`, `gate_check.rs:206`).

**Inert or tolerant configuration.**
- `worktree.mode` with `JIT_WORKTREE_MODE`, `[global_operations]`, `[locks]` and `[events]` are parsed and merged, but only the `config show` printer reads them (`main.rs:6800-6900`).
- Each default is written twice: once in a per-layer accessor (`config.rs:1335-1428`) and once in a `Merged*` accessor (`config.rs:2009-2172`).
- `docs/reference/configuration.md:582` documents them as "Parsed compatibility fields".
- `JitConfig` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so removed keys and typos load silently. A test asserts "stale config must still load" (`config.rs:2730`).
- `agent.toml` tolerates a legacy `[behavior]` block (`agent_config.rs:21`). Rule selectors accept the aliases `has-doc-type` and `doc_type` (`declarations/rules.rs:237,1110`).
- `config::AgentConfig` and `AgentIdentity` (`config.rs:1437`) are used only by tests. Tests exercise a `cfg(test)` copy of `resolve_agent_id` (`agent_config.rs:122`).

**A superseded profile manifest wire.**
- Both shipped profiles declare `manifest-version = 1` (`profiles/jit-default/manifest.toml:10`, `profiles/jit-dogfood/manifest.toml:4`), while `docs/reference/profiles.md:93-99` says new packages use version 2 and the decoder still accepts version 1. Twelve files under `crates/` and `scripts/` still spell version 1.
- Version 1 decoding parses the TOML four times and hashes package identity differently from version 2 (`profile/wire.rs:71-180`).

**Shims left by finished cutovers.**
- `list_issues` sweeps `.jit/issues/` once per process for retired read-lock sidecars (`storage/json.rs:1317`). The sweep misses short-id sidecars, and 19 `.lock` files remain in this repository. The `read_issues` trait method exists only to keep the sweep out of one caller.
- The lifecycle-timestamp backfill ships a `migrate` command, `commands/migrate.rs`, `Event::LifecycleTimestampsBackfilled`, `MutationIntent::RepairIssueLifecycle` and `derive_lifecycle_timestamps`. Its cost is O(issues × events).
- `State::from_str` accepts `open` and `inprogress` as aliases (`domain/types.rs:162-164`).
- The gate fields `auto` and `example_integration` are "deprecated authored field preserved during round trips" (`declarations/gates.rs:188`). `add_gate_definition` is reached only by tests.
- `archived_from` keeps a fallback for archived records that lack it (`domain/types.rs:484`). All 41 archived records in this repository carry it.
- The mermaid exporter declares `classDef open` and has no class for `backlog`, `gated` or `rejected` (`visualization.rs:224-228`).
- Source-scan tests assert the absence of retired file paths, function names and event tags (`tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:1283,1412,1430`).
- `domain/mod.rs` re-exports `types::*` "for backward compatibility". Callers use both paths: about 546 references go through the facade and 339 through `domain::types::`, 333 of them in the test-only `fixture_issue` helper. `domain/mod.rs` and `lib.rs` re-export other domain submodules as well.

**Dead output, domain, storage and UI surface.**
- In output: the `output_message!` and `output_json!` macros, `JsonError::invalid_state`, `invalid_priority` and `gate_validation_failed`, `ExitCode::all_codes_documentation`, and `OutputContext::print_error`, `is_quiet` and `is_json` have no callers, nor do `JsonError::from_code_text` and `ExitCode::description`; `schema.rs:835` hand-copies the exit-code descriptions instead. Six `allow(dead_code)` attributes in `output.rs` sit on these items; they suppress nothing, because `output` is a public library module.
- In domain: `KindScope::parse` and `parse_for` with `ItemError::InvalidScope`; `HierarchyError`, whose only constructed variant (`type_taxonomy.rs:231`) every caller discards, and `ConfigError::DuplicateType`, which is never constructed; `detect_membership_issues`, which is test-only and leaves `ValidationIssue::InvalidMembershipReference` unreachable; `State::is_closed`; `MinimalIssue::state_symbol`, a presentation helper in the domain with one caller (`main.rs:2088`) and an identical twin in `output.rs:1607`; the unused `DocumentReference` builders; `LabelNamespaces::contains`; and `GateRunStatus::Skipped`, which is never constructed.
- `errors::not_in_git_repo` has no caller. `DocFormatAdapter::rewrite_links` defaults to `unimplemented!()` (`document/adapter.rs:48`).
- `ContainerDestinationState` has six variants for three outcomes (`domain/artifact_classifier.rs:244`).
- The reference-page renderers compile into adopter builds, although only the test-support `generated_artifacts` module calls them.
- `FileLocker` repeats one poll loop three times and keeps test-only `try_*` methods under `allow(dead_code)` (`storage/lock.rs:213-346`).
- `with_mutation_interruptions` has a `cfg` twin (`storage/json.rs:455,475`). `InMemoryStorage` carries stale `allow(dead_code)` attributes (`storage/memory.rs:34,68`).
- In `repository_state`, `neutral_files` has no caller, `default_rule_membership_diff` is `allow(dead_code)`, and `mod.rs:41-99` holds `cfg` re-export twins.
- No module imports `web/src/types/hierarchy.ts`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The bracket breakdown module, `validate_integrity_silent` with its private helpers, and `drift::enforcement_drift` are deleted, and no test references them.
- [hard] REQ-02: Repository capture carries no linked-worktree evidence. No capture-spec entry, image field, evidence type or gate-evidence field for it remains, and capturing an image never resolves worktree paths.
- [hard] REQ-03: Configuration declares no `worktree.mode`, `JIT_WORKTREE_MODE`, `[global_operations]`, `[locks]` or `[events]`. Config commands neither print nor check them, the configuration reference does not mention them, and each remaining configuration default is stated once.
- [hard] REQ-04: Loading `config.toml`, `agent.toml` or rule declarations fails on an unknown key with an error that names it. No serde field alias remains in configuration, agent or rule declaration types.
- [hard] REQ-05: One agent configuration type exists, and the agent-id resolver that tests exercise is the function production calls.
- [hard] REQ-06: Profile manifests have one wire version. Both shipped profiles and every fixture declare version 2, the decoder rejects any other version, and package identity has one hashing scheme.
- [hard] REQ-07: The read-lock sidecar sweep and the `read_issues` storage method are deleted. Listing issues creates, rewrites or removes no file other than the storage's own index lock.
- [hard] REQ-08: The lifecycle-timestamp backfill is deleted: the `migrate` command, the migration module, the backfill event variant, the repair mutation intent and the derivation function. An event log that still holds a backfill record parses without error.
- [hard] REQ-09: Lifecycle states parse only from their canonical tokens, and `open` and `inprogress` are rejected wherever a state is accepted.
- [hard] REQ-10: Gate declarations have no `auto` or `example_integration` field. Automation is read from `mode` alone, the projected checker reference shows no `auto` key, and tests define gates through the production definition path.
- [hard] REQ-11: An archived issue record without `archived_from` is invalid, and no legacy-record fallback remains in effective-terminal-state or revive logic.
- [hard] REQ-12: The mermaid exporter declares exactly one class per lifecycle state, derived from the state enumeration.
- [hard] REQ-13: No test asserts the absence of retired file paths, function names or event tags. Structural tests assert current ownership only.
- [hard] REQ-14: Each domain type is imported through one path, and no re-export is justified as backward compatibility.
- [hard] REQ-15: Every output macro, `JsonError` constructor, `ExitCode` helper and `OutputContext` method has a production caller.
- [hard] REQ-16: None of these remain: item-kind scope string parsing and its error variant, taxonomy hierarchy and duplicate-type errors, membership-issue detection and its validation-issue variant, the closed-state predicate, the minimal-issue state symbol, the unused document-reference builders, label-namespace containment, the skipped gate-run status, and the not-in-git-repo error helper.
- [hard] REQ-17: Library code contains no `unimplemented!()`, and document adapters expose no link-rewrite method.
- [hard] REQ-18: Git revision access exposes no query that only tests call. Its error type implements `Clone`, and no hand-written error clone remains.
- [hard] REQ-19: Claim commands carry no unused storage type parameter, and no uncalled lease check remains.
- [hard] REQ-20: A gate that is not required is reported through one typed error. Gate presets hold no validation-rule constructor, and no gate-checker entry point that only tests call and no single-line passthrough remains.
- [hard] REQ-21: Container-destination classification has one variant per outcome it produces. An artifact location that was never inspected is an evidence error, never a default value.
- [hard] REQ-22: Reference-page renderers compile only into builds that include the generated-artifact checks.
- [hard] REQ-23: The file lock has one poll loop. The non-blocking lock variants and the lock-path accessor exist only in test builds.
- [hard] REQ-24: Storage and `repository_state` contain no `cfg` twin of a function or re-export, no `allow(dead_code)` on a public item, and no uncalled scaffold or membership-diff function.
- [hard] REQ-25: Every web UI source module is imported by the application or its tests.
- [hard] REQ-26: The coordination lease limits resolve through one resolver. The values `config show` reports equal the values `claim acquire` enforces, the user and system layers do not apply to lease policy, and the configuration reference carries no carve-out for these limits.
- [hard] REQ-27: Configuration reads no user or system `config.toml` layer: no code reads `~/.config/jit/config.toml` or `/etc/jit/config.toml`, `config set` has no global scope, and the configuration reference lists only repository-level files and the environment.

## Notes

- Serves `@/charter/D-18` (remove mechanism) and `@/inv/canonical-cutover`. The project is greenfield, so no deleted shim needs a migration boundary.
- Deleting the git2-based reference check and the test-only git queries shrinks the surface that `@/charter/D-21` consolidates.
- Each removal deletes its tests, or rewrites them against the surviving path (`@/inv/orthogonal-tests`). Stale prose that names a deleted item is removed in the same change (`@/inv/essential-code-prose`).
- The 19 stale `.jit/issues/*.lock` sidecars in the primary checkout are gitignored runtime residue, not repository content, so no criterion covers them (steward ruling). They are 0-byte files from the retired read-lock mechanism, and deleting them is manual housekeeping outside this epic's graph.
- REQ-26 is a steward-ruled scope addition (2026-10-21). It extends to the coordination lease limits the single-resolver pattern that bedf0962 set for lease enforcement: `config show` merges `max_indefinite_leases_per_agent`/`_per_repo` across the repository, user and system layers (`config.rs:1988-2026`), while `claim acquire` reads only the repository file (`commands/claim.rs:107-111`).
- REQ-27 is a steward-ruled scope addition (2026-10-22). Once REQ-26 made lease policy repository-only, the user and system `config.toml` layers had no remaining reader (`EffectiveConfig::layered` served only `coordination()`), leaving `config set --global` writing a file nothing reads. The agent identity file `~/.config/jit/agent.toml` is a separate mechanism and is unaffected.
title: Remove dead code and compatibility shims across the workspace
